subject: Logic
title: Einstein's Train
description: A fast breakdown of Einstein's Train for builders.

hook.text: Lightning strikes both ends of a moving train at once. A person on the platform agrees. A rider on the train doesn't.

buildup.text: Einstein used this thought experiment to demonstrate that simultaneity is relative to the observer's motion.

discovery.text: The rider moves toward one flash and away from the other, so the light reaches her eyes at different times.

twist.text: Both observers are correct in their own reference frame. There is no absolute now shared across the universe.

climax.text: This demolished Newton's absolute time and became a pillar of special relativity.

punchline.text: Same event, different times. Both are right.

quiz.question: What does Einstein's train experiment show?
options: Simultaneity is relative to the observer's motion
